tagline: A country loop that a new city was founded to keep.
intro: The loop runs 29 miles through a quiet corner of metropolitan Atlanta in south Fulton County, much of it on Cochran Mill Road and Hutcheson Ferry Road, over rolling hills and forested ridges and past pastures. The east side of Cochran Mill Park keeps the ruins of the old mill and the old millpond.

Much of this country is now the city of Chattahoochee Hills, incorporated in 2007 so its residents could hold the zoning and keep the land rural. Its plan sets aside 70 percent of the city as forest and farm for good. The state's bicycle guide to the byway sends riders to Smith's Store in the old Rico community to put air in their tires.

moments.title: Serenbe
moments.text: A short way off the loop, a village built so that every house has a front porch and none has a backyard, all of them facing a shared green and its trails.

moments.title: Rivertown
moments.text: The community takes its name from the Chattahoochee River, which runs along the northwest edge of this hill country.

sources.label: Georgia DOT, South Fulton Scenic Byway Bicycle Guide
